identity.title: Homomorphism Expressivity of Spectral Invariant Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Characterize the expressive power of spectral invariant GNNs through homomorphism expressivity.

gap.claim: The theoretical contribution of spectral invariants to GNNs remains incompletely understood despite their practical use.

contributions.claim: A homomorphism-expressivity analysis of spectral invariant GNNs, including exact counting of a class of tree-like graphs called parallel trees.
A quantitative expressiveness hierarchy across architectural variants, with analysis of GNN depth and subgraph-counting capabilities.
An extension of the analysis to higher-order GNNs addressing an open question from prior work.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper claims to significantly extend prior hierarchy work and settle its open questions, while also answering an open question concerning higher-order GNN expressivity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a proof that spectral invariant GNNs can exactly homomorphism-count parallel trees.
The authors report that their results establish a quantitative hierarchy across architectural variants and clarify the effects of GNN depth and subgraph-counting capabilities.
The authors report extending the analysis to higher-order GNNs and answering an open question raised in prior work.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph spectra are presented as structural features used to enhance GNNs, while their theoretical role remains incompletely understood.
The paper studies the question using homomorphism expressivity and aims for a quantitative analysis.
It proves exact homomorphism counting for a class of tree-like graphs termed parallel trees.
The result is connected to architectural hierarchies, depth, and subgraph-counting capabilities.
The analysis is generalized to higher-order GNNs, addressing an open question from prior work.

source_observation.claim: The abstract frames the central theoretical question through a specific expressivity lens and then states a concrete exact-counting result.

lessons.interpretation: A sharply defined capability can make an abstract's problem-to-result connection easy to evaluate.
lessons.application: Frame another architecture paper around one formal capability, then state the strongest precisely scoped guarantee for that capability.
lessons.exception: This approach is unsuitable when the work is primarily empirical or lacks a natural formal capability measure.

unknowns: The abstract does not define parallel trees or specify the assumptions and architectural variants under which exact counting holds.
The quantitative hierarchy, depth dependence, and higher-order results are stated without numerical or formal details.
The abstract does not specify the precise open questions settled or the comparison baseline used.
